title: Man. Post. Cap. II §XIX: Garissoles on Socinians; Placeus — Socinus denies in word, affirms in deed
pass_a_gloss: GAR. Finally the Socinians expressly deny the imputation of Adam's sin, and yet acknowledge that we on account of our sin are held in the same place as if we had committed Adam's actual disobedience, because to be sure they have acknowledged that the imputation of sin so explained is no imputation of the true name. PLAC. Here too the desire of traducing us has poured darkness on the mind of the Learned Man. For he says the Socinians acknowledge that we on account of our sin are held in the same place as if we had committed Adam's actual disobedience itself. Which is false. For they want us indeed to be held in the same place with Adam, but not on account of our sin (for they acknowledge no sin inhering in us from the origin) but because we were begotten by him, and the same judgment is made of children as of the father. And so our view is away from their opinion by the whole heaven. But as for the rest, Socinus denies the imputation of Adam's sin in words, and posits it in the thing. For if the same judgment is of the son as of the Father, and this one is judged a sinner and worthy of punishment, the son also is judged worthy of punishment: that one indeed because he himself sinned, this one truly because his father sinned. Which, by the Learned Man's own witness, is to impute the father's sin to the son, and indeed by immediate imputation; inasmuch as Socinus denies hereditary corruption, without which mediate imputation cannot be. Add that the same death is inflicted on Adam's posterity and on Adam. But the infliction of punishment itself is for the Learned Man the imputation of sin. In reality therefore Socinus denies the mediate imputation which I acknowledge; the immediate which I impugn he denies only verbally, but in the thing itself he affirms.
pass_b_english: Garissoles: Last, the Socinians flatly deny that Adam's sin is imputed, yet still say that because of our own sin we stand where we would stand if we had done Adam's actual disobedience—because they treat that sort of 'imputation' as no real imputation at all. Placeus: Again the urge to blacken us has fogged the learned man's mind. He claims the Socinians admit we are held, because of our sin, as if we had done Adam's actual disobedience. False. They do put us in Adam's place—but not for our sin (they grant no birth-inhering sin). They do it because we were begotten by him, and children get the father's judgment. Heaven and earth lie between that and our view. For the rest: Socinus denies Adam's sin-imputation in speech and installs it in substance. If son and Father share one judgment, and the father is judged a sinner worthy of punishment, the son is judged worthy too—the one for his own sin, the other for his father's. On the learned man's own showing, that imputes the father's sin to the son, and immediately—because Socinus denies hereditary corruption, without which mediate imputation cannot stand. The same death falls on Adam and on his posterity; and for the learned man, inflicting punishment is itself imputing sin. So in fact Socinus denies the mediate imputation I grant, and only verbally denies the immediate imputation I oppose—while affirming it in the deed.
source_text: GAR. Denique Socinistae imputationem peccati Adae exerte negant, & agnoscunt tamen nos propter nostrum peccatum eodem loco haberi, ac si Adami actualem inobedientiam commisissemus, quia nimirum imputationem peccati sic explicatam agnoverunt, nullam esse veri nominis imputationem. PLAC. Hic quoque nos traducendi cupido tenebras offudit animo Viri Docti. Ait enim Socinistas agnoscere nos propter nostrum peccatum eodem loco haberi, ac si Adami actualem ipsam inobedientiam commisissemus. Id quod falsum est. Volunt enim nos quidem eodem cum Adamo loco haberi, at non propter peccatum nostrum (peccatum enim ab origine nobis inhaerens nullum agnoscunt) sed quia sumus ab eo procreati, & de liberis idem quod de patre judicium sit. Itaque ab eorum sententia abest nostra toto caelo. Caeterum imputationem peccati Adami Socinus verbis negat, re ponit. Nam si idem sit de filio quod de Patre judicium, & hic judicatur peccator & dignus poena, judicatur etiam poena dignus esse filius: Ille quidem quia ipse peccavit, hic vero quia ejus pater peccavit. Id quod, ipso Viro Docto teste, est peccatum patris filio imputare, & quidem imputatione immediata; quippe cum haereditariam corruptionem neget Socinus, sine qua mediata imputatio esse non potest. Adde quod eadem mors infligitur posteris Adami & Adamo. Ipsa autem poenae inflictio est Viro Docto peccati imputatio. Revera igitur Socinus negat imputationem mediatam quam agnosco; immediatam quam impugno verbotenus tantum negat, re autem ipsa affirmat.
